intro: The register offsets below are a stable ABI.
No register was removed. Every word still decodes, and RW words still store.
The LiteX product maps the 64 KiB window at `0x9000_0000`.
Writes to read-only fields are ignored. Unmapped offsets read 0.
`SLVERR` is never raised: every access answers OKAY.
Reserved read-only bits read 0. Reserved R/W bits store what is written.
Plain-RW words read from a write-through shadow RAM.
After reset, `*READY` stays low for about 513 clocks. The defaults ROM loads the shadow meanwhile.
64-bit reads are not atomic on the bus. For time of day, use the snapshot latch.
`VERSION` tracks the map: additive changes bump minor, breaking ones major.
The protocol processor runs the control plane, not this block.
`KL_pp_shadow` wraps it; these registers are its CSR projection.
The AEM descriptor tree has no CSR here. The processor fetches it from main memory.
Queue 4 is the highest priority, queue 0 the lowest.

table: **A restore genuinely completed**: the writer is live and the walk read records out of a validated image
**Blank media behind a validated image**: the store is real but held nothing this walk could use. Not a failure: Milan permits an entity that has never been bound

**Torn read-back, or a BLIND walk**: the walk aborted and the whole image was discarded, or at some cycle of the walk no validated image stood behind the device face, so what it read was the blank answer. The blind verdict is latched per walk in `KL_pp_shadow.sv`: validating the image after the walk does not restore anything, so it cannot clear it
**No writer has answered and the walk ran blind**: what a build whose firmware has not configured the backing store reports, `0x5B00_008C`

soc_registers.ppmem_desc_req: descriptor-image read bridge: `[31:16]` accesses **ISSUED** (one per bus access, counted at its start, not per held cycle), `[15:0]` accesses the bus **ACKED** without `err`
soc_registers.ppmem_desc_fault: `[31:16]` accesses answered with **err**, `[15:0]` accesses the watchdog **abandoned** with no answer at all
soc_registers.ppmem_resp_req: AECP response-buffer read+write bridge, same two fields. This face writes as well as reads: a write that faults voids the response rather than putting a half-written one on the wire
soc_registers.ppmem_resp_fault: same two fields as `desc_fault`, for the response bridge
soc_registers.ppmem_stat: live state, not counts: `[0]` descriptor bridge **poisoned** (a timed-out access is still owed an answer; the next answer it collects is discarded), `[1]` descriptor bridge is driving `cyc`/`stb` **right now**, `[2]` response bridge poisoned, `[3]` response bridge driving `cyc`/`stb`, `[4]` the **LiteDRAM DFI hand-off has been seen** (see below), `[31:24]` constant presence tag `0x5B` -- the same tag as `PP_STAT`, and the register to read first: `0` here means the gateware predates this bank, which is otherwise indistinguishable from four zeroed counters
soc_registers.milan_mac_phy_crg_reset: PHY reset of the port the image is built for (`--eth-port`): the PHY clock/reset block's `_reset` storage, which drives the PHY reset pin. This is the PHY reset; `PHY_RESET` (0x11C) is inert. `ETH_GUARD` does not gate it at this head.
soc_registers.milan_mac_phy_mdio_w: Software bit-bang MDIO write register (clock, output enable, data).
soc_registers.milan_mac_core_preamble_crc: LiteEth status, reset 1: the MAC core inserts and checks preamble and CRC.
soc_registers.milan_mac_loopback: 1 = internal MAC TX to MAC RX loopback.
soc_registers.milan_mac_link_status: Link, speed and duplex published by firmware; mirrored into `MAC_STATUS` (0x110). Reset: link up, 1000 Mb/s on GMII (100 on MII), full duplex.

soc_notes: The bridge bank sits on the CSR window's last page.
Its counters saturate at `0xFFFF`. Read that as at least 65,535.

table: the bridges are **held off the bus**: the BIOS has not handed the DFI back to the LiteDRAM controller yet, so both answer `err` without touching the bus. Expected between FPGA configuration and the end of `sdram_init`, and a standing `0` here means the BIOS never got that far
the bridge **never asked the bus**. The bus is not the fault: look at the processor's request face (`PP_DIAG` `0x930`, the side-port snapshot)
every access completed. If the image is still invalid the fault is upstream of the bus: the descriptor image itself, or its base
an access is **outstanding right now**. `stat[1]`/`stat[3]` say which face is still holding `cyc`/`stb`; it will become a `timed_out` when the watchdog expires
the interconnect answered `err` (LiteX raises `err` **with** `ack`, so a failed access is an answer, not a silence). A descriptor fetched this way is refused, never served
the access was **never answered** and the watchdog abandoned it. `stat[0]`/`stat[2]` show the master poisoned until the memory pays the answer it still owes

PP_CTRL.name: Processor control
PP_CTRL.purpose: Entity enable and the restore-walk start.

fields.PP_ENABLE: **entity enable**, ORed with `ADP_CTRL[0]` (`0x600`); either bit starts the plane.
fields.PP_RESTORE_GO: `restore_go`: start the NVM boot-restore walk against the saved-state backing store (`KL_nvm_backend` behind the processor's NVM device face, [design page](docs/design/SAVED_STATE_FASTCONNECT.md) sections 4, 8 and 9). Until firmware has configured AND validated a record image through `PP_NVM_SEL`/`PP_NVM_DATA` the face answers blank flash (reads `0xFF`, writes accepted and discarded, erase completes), so the walk completes with **zero records** and `restore_fail` set. **Validate the image first, then set this bit**: the verdict is latched per walk, and validating afterwards restores nothing. **Set it on every boot** (processor pin `a8f8ce81`, its issue 92): the processor holds its ACMP listener from reset until the walk ends, so a boot that never sets it never answers an ACMP listener command. Since processor pin `d352bbaa` it also holds AECP until the D3 walk's terminal, and that walk proves the AEM image first: **load and CRC-check the AEM image before this bit**, or the restore ends CLOSED (`PP_STAT[16]`) and AECP stays held until reset. Every restore wait is bounded by `NVM_RS_TMO_CYC_P` (20 ms) and the whole restore by `NVM_RS_AGG_CYC_P` (1,000 ms from this bit), both derived from the clock, so a device face that never answers ends the walks with `restore_fail` set; wait for `restore_done` OR `PP_STAT[16]`, since CLOSED never raises done

fields.PP_RS_CAUSE: The D3 walk's first abort cause, valid with `[3]`: 1 torn, 2 device error, 3 deadline, 5 passes disagree, 6 descriptor fault, 7 image not proven.
fields.PP_RESTORE_RB: A pass-1 abort rolled the stores back to DEFAULTS.
fields.PP_RESTORE_CLOSED: The D3 walk ended CLOSED: fail, never done, AECP held until reset.
fields.PP_NVM_VERDICT: Verdict code of the last image offered.
fields.PP_NVM_PEND: Accepted work no verified slot holds and `nvm_dirty` does not report. A durable reading needs it at 0.
fields.PP_NVM_IMG_VALID: Firmware validated the image in the window.
fields.PP_NVM_STALE: `nvm_backed` was true since reset and is now false, and the loss is not made good.
fields.PP_NVM_DIRTY: The image holds committed changes no flash slot yet holds.
fields.PP_NVM_BLANK: The completed restore validated zero records and none failed.
fields.PP_NVM_BACKED: Live evidence: a writer answered within `T-NVM-WRITER-ALIVE` and no unrevoked failure is outstanding.
fields.PP_ERR: The last side-port access returned an error.
fields.PP_NVM_ALARM: A record producer exhausted its three write attempts. Reset-sticky.
fields.PP_RESTORE_FAIL: A walk failed or ran blind, or the map restore rolled back to its reset set.
fields.PP_RESTORE_DONE: Both boot walks sequenced to COMPLETE or DEFAULTS and the map restore ended. Not the same as succeeded.
